summary: Boxer, Calegari and Gee prove that GL_n(Z) has nonzero cuspidal cohomology for n = 79, 105 and 106 (Theorem B). Equivalently, there are cuspidal automorphic representations of GL_n/Q of level one and weight zero for these n, the first for any n > 1; the Fermigier–Miller range shows that the smallest such n satisfies 27 ≤ n ≤ 79. The method is a change of weight. Starting from Sym^{n−1} of a level-one eigenform f (Newton–Thorne), a lift of Sym^{n−1}ρ̄_f that is crystalline with Hodge–Tate weights 0, …, n−1 and unramified outside p is produced with Bellovin–Gee's dimension bound and the Khare–Wintenberger method, and shown automorphic by polarized automorphy lifting. The ordinary case (Theorem 2.1, needing ρ̄_f|G_{Q_p} split) gives n = 105, 106 from the weight-26 form at p = 107. The non-ordinary case (Theorem 3.1, via Harris's tensor product trick and Thorne's automorphy lifting with p | n) gives n = 79 from a weight-38 form at p = 79. The atlas plans the symmetric powers (ML.3), Galois representations and local–global compatibility (AG2, R19), the general deformation theory, and relative Lie algebra cohomology (AF.1). It lacks cuspidal cohomology, the archimedean analysis of GL_n(R), the polarized automorphy lifting and finiteness theorems of Thorne and BLGGT, G-valued deformation rings, adequacy for p | n, and the level-one change of weight itself. The extraction routes these to two Part IIs (of ModularityAndLanglandsExtensions and of PotentialAutomorphyInfrastructure) and to sources of eight existing layers, and records eight source issues: four misprints (a parameter, two citations, and θ for θ′), three gaps (oddness for GO_n, level one at p in Theorem 3.1, level one in Remark 2.5) and one error (p = 151 in Remark 3.3).

items.name: No modular forms of level one and weight two
items.statement: There is no nonzero cuspidal modular form of level N = 1 (for SL_2(Z)) and weight k = 2; indeed every modular form of weight 2 for SL_2(Z) is zero.
items.note: Read at Mathlib 082e2d3, Mathlib/NumberTheory/ModularForms/LevelOne/DimensionFormula.lean:245: Module.rank ℂ (ModularForm 𝒮ℒ 2) = 0. A cusp form is in particular a modular form.

items.name: The cuspidal cohomology of GL_2(Z) vanishes
items.statement: H^i_cusp(GL_2(Z), C) = 0 for every i, in particular for i = 1. The paper derives this from the absence of cusp forms of level one and weight two through the Eichler–Shimura isomorphism; equivalently it is the case n = 2 of Remark 1.2(3), because a cuspidal automorphic representation of GL_2/Q of level one and weight zero is the same as the representation generated by a normalised Hecke eigenform in S_2(SL_2(Z)).
items.note: The vanishing input is library (PAPER-BOXER-CALEGARI-GEE-25/no-weight-two-cusp-forms-level-one). The translation needs either the Eichler–Shimura isomorphism H^1_cusp(SL_2(Z), C) ≅ S_2 ⊕ conj(S_2) (ModularSymbolsPadicLFunctions:L0 plans the Eichler–Shimura period maps) or the GL_2/Q dictionary of AutomorphicFormsOnReductiveGroups:AF.5 together with Remark 1.2(3). Routed with the level-one cohomology layer.

items.name: Level one and weight zero
items.statement: A cuspidal automorphic representation π of GL_n(A_Q) has level one if π_p is unramified for every prime p, and weight zero if π_∞ has the same infinitesimal character as the trivial representation of GL_n(R).
items.note: Unramified local components and infinitesimal characters are planned in AutomorphicFormsOnReductiveGroups AF.2 and AF.4; this item names the combination used throughout the paper. In the Galois normalisation of [BLGGT14, Thm 2.1.1(3)] weight zero means Hodge–Tate weights 0, 1, …, n−1.

items.name: The two level-one locally symmetric spaces of GL_n/Q
items.statement: For K_∞ equal to O(n) or SO(n), the quotient GL_n(Q)\GL_n(A)/K_∞GL_n(Ẑ) is identified with the quotient of the connected contractible symmetric space GL_n(R)/O(n) (positive definite symmetric matrices) by GL_n(Z) when K_∞ = O(n), and by SL_n(Z) when K_∞ = SO(n).
items.note: ALS.0 constructs the symmetric space and decomposes adelic quotients into arithmetic components; AA.4 plans strong approximation, which with det(GL_n(Ẑ)) = Ẑ^× and class number one gives GL_n(A) = GL_n(Q)GL_n(R)GL_n(Ẑ). Check: GL_n(R)/SO(n) has two components exchanged by elements of GL_n(Z) of determinant −1, so the SO(n) quotient is SL_n(Z)\GL_n(R)^+/SO(n) ≅ SL_n(Z)\(GL_n(R)/O(n)).

items.name: GL_n(Z) versus SL_n(Z)
items.statement: If n is odd then GL_n(Z) = SL_n(Z) × {±1} and the two level-one spaces are equal (−1 acts trivially on GL_n(R)/O(n)); if n is even, the SL_n(Z)-quotient is a double cover of the GL_n(Z)-quotient.
items.note: Elementary. For n even, −1 ∈ SL_n(Z) and GL_n(Z) = SL_n(Z) ⋊ ⟨diag(−1,1,…,1)⟩; 'double cover' is meant in the orbifold sense.

items.name: Cuspidal cohomology of GL_n(Z) and SL_n(Z)
items.statement: H^*_cusp(GL_n(Z), C) and H^*_cusp(SL_n(Z), C) are the subspaces of the cohomology of the two level-one locally symmetric spaces (PAPER-BOXER-CALEGARI-GEE-25/level-one-symmetric-spaces) consisting of the classes represented by harmonic cusp forms.
items.note: No layer of the atlas plans cuspidal cohomology. AutomorphicSpectralTheory:AS.5 owns the comparison of relative Lie algebra cohomology of automorphic forms with the cohomology of the quotient and warns that ordinary cohomology is not cusp cohomology; this general notion (for any reductive group, level and algebraic coefficients, with Borel's injectivity into ordinary cohomology) is routed there. PAPER-FU-24 (partial) proposes the same notion in its proposed Part II WeightAspectAutomorphicMultiplicity (item cuspidal-support-dictionary); it should have one owner, which the other imports.

items.name: Relative Lie algebra cohomology
items.statement: For a (g, K)-module V, H^*(g, K; V) is the cohomology of the complex Hom_K(∧^•(g/k), V) [BW00, I.5]; here g = sl_n or gl_n and K = O(n) or SO(n).
items.note: AF.1 defines relative Lie algebra cochains Hom_K(∧^q(g/k), V) and handles disconnected K via its component group. Mathlib has only low-degree Lie algebra cochains (LieModule.Cohomology.twoCochain, Mathlib/Algebra/Lie/Cochain.lean:46), not relative cohomology.

items.name: Cuspidal cohomology at level one as relative Lie algebra cohomology
items.statement: There is a commutative diagram whose rows ⊕_π H^*(sl_n, O(n); π_∞) → H^*_cusp(GL_n(Z), C) and ⊕_π H^*(sl_n, SO(n); π_∞) → H^*_cusp(SL_n(Z), C) are isomorphisms and whose vertical maps are injections (restriction from O(n) to SO(n) on the left, pull-back along the covering on the right); the sums run over the cuspidal automorphic representations π of GL_n/Q of level one and weight zero.
items.note: Borel's theorem specialised to level one and trivial coefficients. Both rows use sl_n (the offprint's diagram was read at 230 dpi); with gl_n each summand would acquire a factor ∧^•(z^*) from the centre. HR20 and Clo90 were not read (not openly available); the statement is taken from the paper.

items.name: Relative cohomology for O(n) as SO(n)-cohomology invariants
items.note: AF.1 handles disconnected K through its finite component group; the identity is the degreewise statement Hom_{O(n)} = (Hom_{SO(n)})^{O(n)/SO(n)} on cochains, exact because the component group has order 2.

items.name: Tempered cohomological representations of GL_n(R), n even
items.statement: If n is even, there is up to isomorphism a unique tempered irreducible representation π_∞ of GL_n(R) with the infinitesimal character of the trivial representation and nonzero relative Lie algebra cohomology; its restriction to GL_n(R)° is the sum of two irreducible representations, and its (gl_n, SO(n))-cohomology is a free C[O(n)/SO(n)] ≅ C[Z/2Z]-module. In particular it has nonzero O(n)/SO(n)-invariants.
items.locator: Remark 1.2, p. 512, citing [Clo90, Lem. 3.14] and its proof
items.note: Local archimedean representation theory; routed to AutomorphicFormsOnReductiveGroups:AF.4 (cohomological representations). The (gl_n, SO(n)) and (sl_n, SO(n)) versions of freeness are equivalent, because the centre contributes a factor ∧^•(z^*) on which O(n) acts trivially. Clo90 not read.

items.name: Tempered cohomological representations of GL_n(R), n odd
items.statement: If n is odd, there are exactly two tempered irreducible representations of GL_n(R) with the infinitesimal character of the trivial representation and nonzero relative Lie algebra cohomology; they differ by the twist by the sign character of GL_n(R), and O(n)/SO(n) acts on the (gl_n, SO(n))-cohomology of one of them trivially and of the other by −1.
items.note: For n odd, O(n) = SO(n) × {±1} with −1 central, so the component group acts through the central character at −1, which the sign twist changes by (−1)^n = −1. Clo90 not read.

items.name: Archimedean components of level-one weight-zero cuspidal representations
items.statement: If π is a cuspidal automorphic representation of GL_n/Q of weight zero, then π_∞ is one of the tempered cohomological representations of PAPER-BOXER-CALEGARI-GEE-25/archimedean-even or archimedean-odd; in particular H^*(sl_n, SO(n); π_∞) ≠ 0.
items.locator: Remark 1.2, p. 512 (used implicitly in the dimension count and in (3))
items.note: Implicit in the paper: π_∞ of a cuspidal π is generic and unitary, and a generic unitary representation of GL_n(R) with regular integral infinitesimal character is tempered (Clozel's purity lemma, [Clo90, Lemme 4.9]; not read). Routed with the archimedean items to AF.4.

items.name: Level one and weight zero force a trivial central character
items.statement: The central character of a cuspidal automorphic representation of GL_n/Q of level one and weight zero is trivial. Consequently, for n odd, only the tempered cohomological π_∞ with trivial central character occurs, and O(n)/SO(n) acts trivially on its cohomology.
items.note: The central character is a Hecke character of Q^×\A^× unramified at every prime, so it factors through Q^×\A^×/Ẑ^× ≅ R_{>0}; weight zero forces its restriction to R_{>0} to be trivial; hence it is trivial.

items.name: Remark 1.2(1)
items.statement: If n is odd, then H^*_cusp(GL_n(Z), C) = H^*_cusp(SL_n(Z), C).

items.name: Remark 1.2(2)
items.statement: If n is even, then dim H^*_cusp(SL_n(Z), C) = 2 dim H^*_cusp(GL_n(Z), C).

items.name: Remark 1.2(3)
items.statement: For every n, the spaces H^*_cusp(GL_n(Z), C) and H^*_cusp(SL_n(Z), C) are nonzero if and only if there exists a cuspidal automorphic representation of GL_n/Q of level one and weight zero.

items.name: No level-one weight-zero forms for 1 < n < 27
items.statement: [Fer96, Cor. 1] for n ≤ 23 and [Mil02, Thm. 1.6] for n < 27: the cuspidal cohomology with constant coefficients H^*_cusp(SL_n(Z), C) vanishes for 1 < n < 27. Equivalently (Remark 1.2), no cuspidal automorphic representation of GL_n/Q of level one and weight zero exists for 1 < n < 27.
items.locator: Section 1, p. 509; [Mil02, Thm 1.6] read in arXiv math/0112196v1
items.note: Miller's statement is for SL_n(Z); Fermigier's is for GL_n(Z). The proofs use the explicit formula and positivity for Rankin–Selberg L-functions L(s, π × π̃) (the Stark–Odlyzko technique). No layer plans this; the Part II imports AnalyticNumberTheory AN.3 (explicit formulas) and AutomorphicLFunctionsAndLocalFactors AL.3 (Rankin–Selberg). Fer96 was not read.

items.name: Theorem B: existence
items.statement: There exist cuspidal automorphic representations of GL_n/Q of level one and weight zero for n = 79, n = 105 and n = 106.
items.locator: Theorem B, p. 510 (proved as Theorem 2.4 and Corollary 3.2)

items.name: Theorem B: cuspidal cohomology
items.statement: H^*_cusp(GL_n(Z), C) ≠ 0 for n = 79, 105 and 106.
items.note: From PAPER-BOXER-CALEGARI-GEE-25/theorem-B-existence and Remark 1.2(3).

items.name: Bounds for the smallest n
items.statement: The smallest n > 1 such that H^i_cusp(GL_n(Z), C) ≠ 0 for some i satisfies 27 ≤ n ≤ 79.
items.note: Lower bound: PAPER-BOXER-CALEGARI-GEE-25/fermigier-miller-vanishing, transferred from SL_n(Z) to GL_n(Z) by the injection of Remark 1.2. Upper bound: Theorem B with n = 79.

items.name: Remark 1.1: conditional existence for infinitely many n
items.statement: Let π be a cuspidal automorphic representation of GL_n/Q of level one and weight zero with n > 1 odd, and let f be a level-one cuspidal eigenform of weight n + 1. For m ≥ 1, if the tensor product π ⊠ Sym^{m−1} f of the conjectural functoriality GL_n × GL_m → GL_{nm} exists and is cuspidal, it is a cuspidal automorphic representation of GL_{nm}/Q of level one and weight zero. So, conditionally on this functoriality, such representations exist for infinitely many n.
items.note: Weight check: the Hodge–Tate weights {a + bn : 0 ≤ a ≤ n−1, 0 ≤ b ≤ m−1} are 0, 1, …, nm−1, each once. The existence of f uses n > 26, which holds by PAPER-BOXER-CALEGARI-GEE-25/fermigier-miller-vanishing (n + 1 even, at least 28). The conjectural functoriality is ModularityAndLanglandsExtensions ML.5's.

items.name: Level-one eigenforms of weight n + 1
items.statement: For every odd n > 26 there is a level-one cuspidal Hecke eigenform of weight n + 1.
items.note: S_{n+1}(SL_2(Z)) ≠ 0 is library: Mathlib's dimension formula (DimensionFormula.lean:250) and rank M_k = 1 + rank S_k for even k ≥ 4 (:171). A simultaneous Hecke eigenvector is Tau Ceti ModularForms Layer 4's good-Hecke simultaneous diagonalisation.

items.name: The p-adic and mod p cyclotomic characters
items.statement: ε: G_Q → Z_p^× is the p-adic cyclotomic character and ε̄ its reduction modulo p.
items.note: Mathlib/NumberTheory/Cyclotomic/CyclotomicCharacter.lean:307 (cyclotomicCharacter L p : (L ≃+* L) →* ℤ_[p]ˣ) and :212 (modularCyclotomicCharacter); apply with L an algebraic closure of Q.

items.name: Galois representations of level-one eigenforms
items.statement: For an eigenform f of level SL_2(Z) and weight k ≥ 2 and a fixed ι_p: C ≅ Q̄_p, ρ_f: G_Q → GL_2(Q̄_p) and ρ̄_f: G_Q → GL_2(F̄_p) are the cohomologically normalised representations attached to f: unramified outside p with the characteristic polynomial of Frobenius given by the Hecke polynomial, and symplectic with multiplier ε^{1−k} (det ρ_f = ε^{1−k}).
items.locator: Section 2, p. 512; proof of Theorem 2.1, p. 513

items.name: Galois representations of regular algebraic polarized cuspidal representations
items.statement: [BLGGT14, Thm. 2.1.1]: for a regular algebraic cuspidal polarized (π, χ) of GL_n(A_F), F CM or totally real, there is a continuous semisimple r_{l,ι}(π): G_F → GL_n(Q̄_l) such that (1) (r_{l,ι}(π), ε^{1−n}r_{l,ι}(χ)) is totally odd and polarized; (2) for v ∤ l, ιWD(r|G_{F_v})^{F-ss} ≅ rec(π_v ⊗ |det|_v^{(1−n)/2}), pure; (3) r is de Rham with HT_τ(r) = {a_{ιτ,1} + n − 1, …, a_{ιτ,n}}; (4) for v | l with π_v having an Iwahori-fixed vector, the same Weil–Deligne compatibility holds, so r|G_{F_v} is semistable, and crystalline if π_v is unramified.
items.locator: Section 2 ('the p-adic Galois representation'), p. 512; proof of Theorem 2.1, p. 515; [BLGGT14, Thm 2.1.1] read in arXiv 1010.2561v4

items.name: Local–global compatibility at l = p for all local components
items.statement: For a regular algebraic conjugate self-dual cuspidal Π of GL_n(A_L), L a CM field, and every place y | l: WD(r_l(Π)|Gal(L̄_y/L_y))^{F-ss} ≅ ι^{−1}L_{n,L_y}(Π_y) (Caraiani, Monodromy and local–global compatibility for l = p, Thm. 1.1). In particular r|G_{L_y} crystalline implies Π_y unramified.
items.locator: Needed for 'level one' in Theorems 2.1 and 3.1 (see source issue E6); Caraiani arXiv 1202.4683v1, Thm 1.1
items.note: Not cited by the paper, which cites [BLGGT14, Thm 2.1.1]; part (4) of that theorem needs an Iwahori-fixed vector. AG2.6 plans the full monodromy comparison at the coefficient prime through the generalised log-crystalline weight spectral sequence, which is Caraiani's argument.

items.name: Theorem 2.1 for n = p − 1
items.statement: Let f be an eigenform of level SL_2(Z) and weight k ≥ 2, and let p > 5 be a prime such that (1) ρ̄_f(G_Q) ⊇ SL_2(F_p); (2) (p − 1, k − 1) = 1; (3) f is ordinary at p; (4) ρ̄_f|G_{Q_p} is semisimple. Then for n = p − 1 there exists a self-dual cuspidal automorphic representation π of GL_n/Q of level one and weight zero whose mod p Galois representation ρ̄_π: G_Q → GL_n(F̄_p) is isomorphic to Sym^{n−1}(ρ̄_f ⊗ ε̄^{(k−2)/2}) = ε̄^{(n−1)(k−2)/2} ⊗ Sym^{n−1}ρ̄_f.
items.note: n = p − 1 is even and G_n = GSp_n.

items.name: Theorem 2.1 for n = p − 2
items.statement: Let f be an eigenform of level SL_2(Z) and weight k ≥ 2, and let p > 5 be a prime such that (1) ρ̄_f(G_Q) ⊇ SL_2(F_p); (2) (p − 1, k − 1) = 1; (3) f is ordinary at p; (4) ρ̄_f|G_{Q_p} is semisimple. Then for n = p − 2 there exists a self-dual cuspidal automorphic representation π of GL_n/Q of level one and weight zero whose mod p Galois representation ρ̄_π: G_Q → GL_n(F̄_p) is isomorphic to Sym^{n−1}(ρ̄_f ⊗ ε̄^{(k−2)/2}) = ε̄^{(n−1)(k−2)/2} ⊗ Sym^{n−1}ρ̄_f.
items.note: n = p − 2 is odd and G_n = GO_n.

items.name: The similitude groups G_n
items.statement: G_n = GSp_n for n even (the similitude group of the standard alternating form J_n) and G_n = GO_n for n odd (the similitude group of the form 1_n), with multiplier character ν: G_n → GL_1; A_n denotes the matrix of the form (1_n for n odd, J_n for n even), and g_n^0 = sp_n or so_n is the Lie algebra of the derived group.
items.note: Mathlib has Sp (Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/SymplecticGroup.lean:101) and O (UnitaryGroup.lean:295) but no similitude groups; Tau Ceti's TauCeti.GLSymplectic is Sp inside GL. PELModuli:M0 constructs the similitude group of a PEL datum (GSp); GO_n is planned nowhere. Routed to ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations G7, which defines polarizations with an actual pairing and multiplier.

items.name: Polarization of symmetric powers
items.statement: Let r: Γ → GL_2(F) preserve an alternating form up to the multiplier μ (i.e. det r = μ). Then Sym^{n−1}r preserves a form up to μ^{n−1}, alternating for n even and symmetric for n odd; so it takes values in G_n(F) with multiplier μ^{n−1}. Applied to ρ̄_f ⊗ ε̄^{(k−2)/2} (multiplier ε̄^{1−k}ε̄^{k−2} = ε̄^{−1}) this gives ρ̄: G_Q → G_n(F) with multiplier ε̄^{1−n} and ρ̄ ≅ ρ̄^∨ε̄^{1−n}; applied to ρ̄_f with n = p it gives Sym^{p−1}ρ̄_f: G_Q → GO_p(F) with multiplier ε̄^{(1−k)(p−1)} = 1 = ε̄^{1−p}.
items.locator: Proof of Theorem 2.1, p. 513; proof of Theorem 3.1, p. 516
items.note: Tau Ceti has symmetric powers of representations (TauCeti/RepresentationTheory/SymmetricPower.lean:47) but not the induced pairing. Routed to ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations G7 (symmetric powers and polarizations).

items.name: Local shape of ρ̄_f for ordinary f
items.statement: If f is ordinary at p (a_p(f) a p-adic unit), then ρ_f|G_{Q_p} is an extension of ψ^{−1}ε^{1−k} by ψ with ψ unramified; so if moreover ρ̄_f|G_{Q_p} is semisimple, ρ̄_f|G_{Q_p} ≅ ψ̄ ⊕ ψ̄^{−1}ε̄^{1−k} for an unramified character ψ̄.
items.note: Deligne's and Mazur–Wiles's description of ρ_f at an ordinary prime; R19.5 includes the ordinary cases required for lifting.

items.name: The local decomposition (2.1.1)
items.statement: Under the hypotheses of Theorem 2.1, with n = p − 1 or p − 2 and ρ̄ = Sym^{n−1}(ρ̄_f ⊗ ε̄^{(k−2)/2}): ρ̄|G_{Q_p} ≅ ⊕_{i=0}^{n−1} ψ̄^{n−1−2i} ε̄^{(n−1)(k−2)/2 − (k−1)i}, and consequently there are unramified characters ψ̄_i (0 ≤ i ≤ n−1) with ρ̄|G_{Q_p} ≅ ⊕_{i=0}^{n−1} ψ̄_i ε̄^{−i} and ψ̄_{n−1−i} = ψ̄_i^{−1}.
items.note: Checked by exact arithmetic: for every prime 7 ≤ p < 200 and every even k < 3p with (p−1, k−1) = 1, the exponents (n−1)(k−2)/2 − (k−1)i mod p−1 are exactly −i for i = 0, …, n−1 (for n = p−2 the missing residue is 1), and the pairing i ↔ n−1−i sends exponent e to −(n−1)−e. The same computation illustrates the introduction's example on p. 511.

items.name: Absolute irreducibility of residual symmetric powers
items.statement: If SL_2(F_p) ⊆ r̄(G_Q) for r̄: G_Q → GL_2(F̄_p) and n ≤ p, then Sym^{n−1}r̄ (and each of its twists) is absolutely irreducible.
items.locator: Proof of Theorem 2.1, p. 513 (see also Lemma 2.2)
items.note: Sym^a of the standard representation of SL_2(F_p) is irreducible for 0 ≤ a ≤ p − 1.

items.name: The deformation ring R of Theorem 2.1
items.statement: Let E/Q_p be finite with ring of integers O and residue field F ⊇ the field of definition of ρ̄. R is the complete local Noetherian O-algebra that is the universal deformation ring for G_n-valued deformations of ρ̄ with multiplier ε^{1−n}, unramified outside p, whose restrictions to G_{Q_p} are crystalline and ordinary with Hodge–Tate weights 0, 1, …, n−1. The local ring at p is the union of the ordinary irreducible components of the crystalline deformation ring ([FKP22, Lem. B.4]).

items.name: Bellovin–Gee lower bound for global deformation rings
items.statement: [BG19, Prop. 4.2.6]: let F be totally real, l > 2, S a finite set of places containing those above l∞, and ρ̄: Gal_{F,S} → G(F) admitting a universal deformation ring (H^0(Gal_{F,S}, g_F) = z_F) that is discrete series and odd ([BG19, Def. 4.2.1]: dim H^0(Gal_{F_v}, g_F^0) = dim G − dim B for all v | ∞) with H^0(Gal_{F,S}, (g_F^0)^*(1)) = 0. Fix inertial types at v ∈ S and regular Hodge types at v | l so that the chosen local rings R_v (non-empty unions of irreducible components) are nonzero. Then the fixed-determinant universal deformation ring R^univ has Krull dimension at least one.
items.locator: Proofs of Theorems 2.1 and 3.1, pp. 513 and 517; [BG19, Prop 4.2.6, Def 4.2.1] read in arXiv 1708.04885v3
items.note: g^0 is the Lie algebra of the derived group of G (BG19 §2). Routed to GlobalGaloisDeformations G7 (polarized dimension-n problems and presentations over completed tensor products of local rings).

items.name: Ordinary components of G-valued crystalline deformation rings
items.statement: [FKP22, Lem. B.4]: for a G-valued residual ρ̄ of G_{F_v} and a weight λ, the λ-ordinary quotient of the lifting ring of Hodge type v_λ is a union of irreducible components; a point factors through it exactly when the lift is ordinary of weight λ (Def. B.2); the same holds for fixed-multiplier lifting rings with dim G^der in place of dim G.
items.locator: Proof of Theorem 2.1, p. 513; [FKP22, Lem. B.4] read in arXiv 2008.12593v5
items.note: Routed to LocalGaloisDeformationRings L7 (ordinary deformation functors and component maps), in the G-valued generality. FKP22 is already queued as PAPER-FAKHRUDDIN-KHARE-PATRIKIS-22.

items.name: An ordinary crystalline lift of ρ̄|G_{Q_p}
items.statement: ρ̄|G_{Q_p} ≅ ⊕_i ψ̄_i ε̄^{−i} has the ordinary crystalline lift ⊕_i [ψ̄_i]ε^{−i} (Teichmüller lifts of the ψ̄_i), which has multiplier ε^{1−n} and Hodge–Tate weights 0, …, n−1; so the local ring at p in the definition of R is nonzero.

items.name: Vanishing of H^0(Q, (g_n^0)^*(1))
items.statement: For p > 3, n ≤ p and SL_2(F_p) ⊆ ρ̄_f(G_Q), with ρ̄ a twist of Sym^{n−1}ρ̄_f: H^0(Q, (g_n^0)^*(1)) = 0. It suffices to show there are no invariants after semisimplification: (g_n^0)^{*,ss} ⊂ gl_n^{*,ss} ≅ gl_n^{ss} ≅ ⊕_{i=0}^{n−1}(Sym^{2i}ρ̄_f)^{ss} ⊗ det(ρ̄_f)^{−i} ⊂ ⊕_{i=0}^{p−1}(Sym^{2i}ρ̄_f)^{ss} ⊗ det(ρ̄_f)^{−i}, whose one-dimensional constituents are self-dual characters, hence different from ε̄^{−1}.
items.locator: Proof of Theorem 2.1, pp. 513–514; reused for so_p in the proof of Theorem 3.1, p. 517

items.name: One-dimensional constituents of Sym^{2i} for SL_2(F)
items.statement: Let F be the finite field with SL_2(F) ⊆ image (acting on F̄_p^2), p odd. For 0 ≤ i ≤ p − 1, the one-dimensional composition factors of Sym^{2i} occur with multiplicity at most one, and only for i = 0, 2i = p + 1 (the latter only when F = F_p) and 2i = 2p − 2.
items.note: Checked with Brauer characters: for SL_2(F_p), p = 7, 11, 13, the trivial constituent occurs in Sym^d (d ≤ 2p−2) exactly for d = 0, p+1, 2p−2, once each; for SL_2(F_{p^2}), p = 5, 7, only for d = 0 and 2p−2. The characters that arise (trivial, det^{−(p−1)/2}, trivial) are self-dual.

items.name: Clebsch–Gordan after semisimplification
items.statement: For V two-dimensional over F̄_p and n ≤ p: End(Sym^{n−1}V)^{ss} ≅ ⊕_{i=0}^{n−1}(Sym^{2i}V)^{ss} ⊗ det^{−i} as representations of any group acting on V.
items.note: Holds for Brauer characters because it holds in characteristic zero; Tau Ceti LieHighestWeight Layer 0 plans the characteristic-zero Clebsch–Gordan for sl_2 only.

items.name: ρ̄ is discrete series and odd
items.statement: ρ̄ satisfies [BG19, Def. 4.2.1] at the real place: for n even (GSp_n) this follows from the multiplier ε̄^{1−n} being odd (the ±1-eigenspaces of ρ̄(c) are Lagrangian); for n odd (GO_n, including n = p in Theorem 3.1) ρ̄(c) = Sym^{n−1} of an odd two-dimensional matrix has eigenvalues +1 and −1 with multiplicities (n+1)/2 and (n−1)/2 up to sign, so dim so_n^{ρ̄(c)} = ((n−1)/2)^2 = dim GO_n − dim B. The Hodge–Tate weights 0, …, n−1 are distinct, so the Hodge type is regular.
items.locator: Proof of Theorem 2.1, p. 514; implicit in the proof of Theorem 3.1, p. 517
items.note: The paper gives only the parity of the multiplier, which does not settle the orthogonal case (source issue E5). Eigenvalue counts checked: (53, 52) for n = 105, (53, 53) for n = 106, (40, 39) for n = 79.

items.name: Components of R have dimension at least one
items.statement: Every irreducible component of R (Theorem 2.1) has Krull dimension at least 1.
items.note: By PAPER-BOXER-CALEGARI-GEE-25/bg19-dimension-bound with l = p, S = {p, ∞}, the ordinary crystalline components at p, and the hypotheses verified by dual-adjoint-invariants-vanish and oddness-for-bg19.

items.name: The auxiliary imaginary quadratic field
items.statement: An imaginary quadratic field F/Q in which p splits and which is linearly disjoint from Q̄^{ker ρ̄}(ζ_p).

items.name: The group 𝒢_n
items.statement: 𝒢_n is the semidirect product of 𝒢_n^0 = GL_n × GL_1 by {1, j}, with j(g, a)j^{−1} = (a g^{−t}, a); its multiplier ν: 𝒢_n → GL_1 sends (g, a) to a and j to −1 ([CHT08, §2.1]).
items.note: Read in [BLGGT14, §1.1] and [BG19, §5.1], which agree. Routed to ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations G7 with the polarization formalism (a 𝒢_n-valued representation of G_{F^+} is a polarized representation of G_F).

items.name: The map ψ ↦ r_ψ and the injection (2.1.2)
items.statement: Given ψ: G_Q → G_n(R), r_ψ: G_Q → 𝒢_n(R) is the composite G_Q → G_n(R) × G_Q/G_F → 𝒢_n(R) of ψ × pr with the injection (2.1.2) G_n × {±1} ↪ 𝒢_n given by r((g, 1)) = (g, ν(g)) and r((g, −1)) = (g, ν(g))·(A_n^{−1}, (−1)^{n+1})j. Its multiplier is that of ψ times δ_{F/Q}^n. One writes r̄ := r_{ρ̄}.
items.note: Checked symbolically: (2.1.2) is a group homomorphism with ν(r((g, s))) = ν(g)s^n, for random similitudes over Q with n = 2, 3, 4, 5. It agrees with the maps r̂_Δ of [BLGGT14, §1.1].

items.name: The deformation ring R_F of Theorem 2.1
items.statement: R_F is the complete local Noetherian O-algebra that is the universal deformation ring for 𝒢_n-valued deformations of r̄ with multiplier ε^{1−n}δ_{F/F^+}^n (here F^+ = Q), unramified outside p, whose restrictions to the places above p are crystalline and ordinary with Hodge–Tate weights 0, 1, …, n−1.

items.name: R_F → R is surjective
items.statement: The association ψ ↦ r_ψ induces a surjection R_F → R. It suffices to check surjectivity on reduced cotangent spaces, which follows because the map of Lie algebras induced by (2.1.2) is a split injection of G_Q-modules, equivalently (as p > 2) of G_F-modules.
items.note: A general lemma about restricting G_n-valued deformations over a totally real field to 𝒢_n-valued ones over a CM quadratic extension, with compatible local conditions; routed to GlobalGaloisDeformations G7.

items.name: (r̄|G_F, μ̄) is ordinarily automorphic
items.statement: The polarized residual representation (r̄|G_F, μ̄) is ordinarily automorphic: by [NT21, Thm. A] Sym^{n−1}π_f is cuspidal automorphic on GL_n(A_Q); it is ι-ordinary because f is ordinary at p; and its base change to F is cuspidal and ι-ordinary.
items.note: ι-ordinarity follows from [BLGGT14, §2.1, remark (7)]: level potentially prime to l and ordinary Galois representation imply ι-ordinary. Cuspidality of the base change holds because ρ̄|G_F is irreducible (F is disjoint from Q̄^{ker ρ̄}).

items.name: Symmetric power functoriality for level-one forms
items.statement: [NT21, Thm. A]: let π be a regular algebraic cuspidal automorphic representation of GL_2(A_Q) of level 1. Then for each n ≥ 2 the symmetric power lifting Sym^{n−1}π exists as a regular algebraic cuspidal automorphic representation of GL_n(A_Q).
items.locator: Section 1, p. 511; proof of Theorem 2.1, p. 514; [NT21, Thm A] read in arXiv 1912.11261v3
items.note: ML.3 integrates Newton–Thorne symmetric-power automorphy. NT21 is already queued as PAPER-NEWTON-THORNE-21.

items.name: Quadratic and cyclic base change
items.statement: Cyclic (in particular quadratic) base change of cuspidal automorphic representations of GL_n from Q to F, and from F to cyclic extensions (Arthur–Clozel), with its effect on Galois representations.
items.locator: Proof of Theorem 2.1, p. 514 ('together with quadratic base change')
items.note: ML.5 registers cyclic base change and automorphic induction with exact hypotheses.

items.name: ι-ordinary and ordinarily automorphic
items.statement: [BLGGT14, §2.1]: a regular algebraic π of weight a is ι-ordinary if for each v | l some Iwahori level of π_v has a nonzero ordinary part, the maximal subspace on which all rescaled operators U^{(j)}_{ι*a,ϖ_v} have l-adic unit eigenvalues; (r, μ) is ordinarily automorphic if it is automorphic via an ι-ordinary (π, χ).
items.note: Routed to the polarized automorphy lifting Part II; PotentialAutomorphyInfrastructure PA.2 owns ordinary parts in the ACC+ (non-polarized) setting.

items.name: Characteristic-zero points of finite O-algebras
items.statement: A complete Noetherian local O-algebra that is finite over O and has Krull dimension at least 1 has a Q̄_p-valued point.
items.locator: Proofs of Theorems 2.1 and 3.1, pp. 515 and 517
items.note: Decomposition node DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra:R03.4/characteristic-zero-points-from-finiteness-and-dimension states exactly this, with the warning that nonzeroness alone is insufficient.

items.name: Finiteness of ordinary polarized deformation rings
items.statement: [Tho12, Thm. 10.2] = [BLGGT14, Thm. 2.4.2]: let F be an imaginary CM field, l odd with ζ_l ∉ F, S a finite set of places of F^+ containing those above l, all split in F; (π, χ) an ι-ordinary RAECSDC representation of GL_n(A_F) unramified outside S with r̄_{l,ι}(π)(G_{F(ζ_l)}) adequate. For the polarized deformation problem with all lifts at v ∈ S, v ∤ l, and ss-ordinary lifts of weight λ at v | l, the universal ring is a finite O-module.
items.locator: Proof of Theorem 2.1, p. 514 (cited as [Tho12, Thm. 10.1]; see source issue E2); read in [Tho12] (author's copy and arXiv 1107.5989v1) and [BLGGT14] arXiv v4
items.note: R_F is a quotient of this ring for S = {p}, so R_F is finite over O.

items.name: Ordinary automorphy lifting
items.statement: [BLGGT14, Thm. 2.4.1] (from [Tho12, Thm. 9.1] for F imaginary; totally real F by base change): let F be CM or totally real, l odd, (r, μ) an n-dimensional algebraic polarized l-adic representation with r̄ irreducible and r̄(G_{F(ζ_l)}) adequate, ζ_l ∉ F, r ordinary at all primes above l, and (r̄, μ̄) ordinarily automorphic. Then (r, μ) is ordinarily automorphic, and of level prime to l if r is crystalline at l.
items.locator: Proof of Theorem 2.1, p. 515; [BLGGT14, Thm 2.4.1] read in arXiv v4
items.note: The paper applies it with F = Q, l = p, r = ρ, μ = ε^{1−n}δ^n_{F/F^+} and prints n = p − 1 where n is meant (source issue E1). The 'level prime to l' clause is what makes π_p unramified in Theorem 2.1.

items.name: The lift ρ of Theorem 2.1 and its automorphy
items.statement: R_F is finite over O, hence so is R; as R has dimension at least 1 it has a Q̄_p-point, giving a lift ρ: G_Q → G_n(Q̄_p) of ρ̄ unramified outside p, with multiplier ε^{1−n}, crystalline and ordinary with Hodge–Tate weights 0, …, n−1. Then ρ is automorphic: there is a self-dual regular algebraic cuspidal π of GL_n(A_Q) with ρ_π ≅ ρ, and π has level one and weight zero.
items.note: Level one away from p uses [BLGGT14, Thm 2.1.1(2)]; at p it uses the level-prime-to-l clause of ordinary-automorphy-lifting; weight zero uses Thm 2.1.1(3); self-duality comes from μ = ε^{1−n}.

items.name: Lemma 2.2: adequacy of small symmetric powers
items.statement: Let p > 5 and r̄: G_Q → GL_2(F̄_p) with SL_2(F_p) ⊆ r̄(G_Q). Then for p − 2 ≤ n ≤ p, the group (Sym^{n−1}r̄)(G_{Q(ζ_p)}) is adequate in the sense of [Tho17, Defn. 2.20].
items.note: Proof: SL_2(F_p) is perfect, so SL_2(F_p) ⊆ r̄(G_{Q(ζ_p)}); by Dickson SL_2(F_q) ⊆ r̄(G_{Q(ζ_p)}) with index prime to p; by [GHT17, Rem. 6.1] it suffices that V = Sym^{n−1}U is adequate for G = SL_2(F_q), which [GHT17, Cor. 9.4] gives since n ≥ p − 2 > (p+1)/2. Routed to ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations G7, as PAPER-NEWTON-THORNE-26 routed its adequacy of small symmetric powers.

items.name: Adequate subgroups
items.statement: [Tho17, Defn. 2.20], taken from [GHT17]: H ⊂ GL_n(K) is adequate if H^1(H, K) = 0 and H^1(H, ad_0) = 0 (ad_0 the quotient of ad by the scalars) and, for every simple K[H]-submodule W ⊂ ad, there is a semisimple σ ∈ H with an eigenvalue α such that tr e_{σ,α}W ≠ 0.
items.locator: Lemma 2.2, p. 515; proof of Theorem 3.1, p. 518
items.note: For p ∤ n this is equivalent to [Tho12, Defn. 2.3]; for p | n only the GHT form can hold. ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations G7 plans adequacy as an explicit cohomological condition; routed there.

items.name: Reduction to the subgroup generated by p-elements
items.statement: [GHT17, Rem. 6.1]: for a finite irreducible G ≤ GL(V), adequacy of (G, V) follows from adequacy of G^+ (the subgroup generated by the p-elements) on V.
items.locator: Lemma 2.2 proof, p. 515; read in arXiv 1405.0043v3

items.name: Adequacy for SL_2(p^r)
items.statement: [GHT17, Cor. 9.4]: a nontrivial absolutely irreducible representation V of G = SL_2(p^r) in characteristic p is adequate unless (i) r = 1 and 1 < dim V = (p ± 1)/2; (ii) p^r ∈ {2, 3, 4} and dim V = p^r; or (iii) p^r = 9 and dim V ∈ {3, 6, 9}.
items.locator: Lemma 2.2 proof, p. 515; read in arXiv 1405.0043v3

items.name: Dickson's classification
items.statement: A finite subgroup H of GL_2(F̄_p) containing SL_2(F_p) contains SL_2(F_q) for some power q of p with p ∤ [H : SL_2(F_q)]; more generally a finite irreducible subgroup of GL_2(F̄_p) has projective image cyclic, dihedral, A_4, S_4, A_5, PSL_2(F_q) or PGL_2(F_q).
items.locator: Lemma 2.2 proof, p. 515; Theorem 3.1 proof, p. 516
items.note: Decomposition node ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.4/dickson-classification-and-the-dyadic-refinement.

items.name: The level-one eigenform of weight 26
items.statement: S_26(SL_2(Z)) is one-dimensional, spanned by f = ΔE_4^2E_6, which is therefore the unique normalised cuspidal Hecke eigenform of level one and weight 26.
items.note: rank M_26 = 26/12 = 2 as 26 ≡ 2 mod 12 (DimensionFormula.lean:250), so rank S_26 = 1 (:171). Δ is ModularForm.discriminant (Discriminant.lean:52), as a cusp form CuspForm.discriminant (:239), E_4 and E_6 are EisensteinSeries/Basic.lean:51, 54. A one-dimensional Hecke-stable space consists of eigenforms; Tau Ceti's IsEigenformAwayFromLevel (ModularForms/Eigenform.lean:65) at N = 1 is the eigenform predicate.

items.name: Coefficients of ΔE_4^2E_6
items.note: Verified by exact integer arithmetic (E_4, E_6 from divisor sums and Δ = q∏(1−q^n)^24 via the pentagonal theorem): a_1, a_2, a_3 = 1, −48, −195804; a_107 as printed; a_2a_3 = a_6 and a_4 = a_2^2 − 2^25. Routed to ComputationalNumberTheory CN.3 (certified q-expansions and Hecke data).

items.name: The mod 107 image of the weight-26 form
items.statement: [SD73, Cor., p. SwD-31]: the image of the mod 107 representation ρ̄ of f = ΔE_4^2E_6 is exactly GL_2(F_107) (the image contains SL_2(F_107), and det ρ̄ = ε̄^{−25} is surjective because (F_107^×)^{25} = F_107^×).
items.note: SD73 (Lecture Notes in Math. 350) was not read. The exceptional primes of the weight-26 form are small primes and 657931 (a factor of the numerator of B_26); 107 is not among them. Routed to ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations R01.4 (residual images of GL_2 representations).

items.name: A companion form of weight 82 at p = 107
items.statement: f admits a companion form of weight p + 1 − k = 82: an eigenform g of level one and weight 82 with ρ̄_f ≅ ε̄^{−25}ρ̄_g (a computation of Elkies recorded in [Gro90, §17]).
items.note: Confirmed independently mod 107: the characteristic polynomials of T_2 and T_3 on S_26 and on S_82, twisted by 2^{81} and 3^{81}, share a common root, and T_107 is invertible on S_26. This agrees with the [CG13] table (p = 107: C[26]). Routed to ComputationalNumberTheory CN.3.

items.name: Companion forms force a split local representation
items.statement: [Gro90, Prop. 13.8(3)] (the easy direction of Gross's companion-form theorem): if an ordinary eigenform f of weight 2 ≤ k ≤ p − 1 has a companion form g of weight p + 1 − k, i.e. ρ̄_g ≅ ρ̄_f ⊗ ε̄^{k−1}, then ρ̄_f|G_{Q_p} is semisimple (tamely ramified).
items.note: Gro90 (Duke 1990) was not read. Argument: ρ̄_f|I_p has sub 1 and quotient ε̄^{1−k}; the companion gives a second invariant line on which I_p acts by ε̄^{1−k} ≠ 1. Routed to SerreWeightAndLevelOptimisation R20.3, which owns the weight theorem whose tame level-one case uses companion forms.

items.name: Theorem 2.4
items.statement: There exist self-dual cuspidal automorphic representations π of GL_n/Q of level one and weight zero for n = 105 and n = 106. In particular H^*_cusp(GL_n(Z), C) ≠ 0 for these n.
items.note: Theorem 2.1 applied to f = ΔE_4^2E_6, k = 26, p = 107: (1) by sd73-image, (2) (106, 25) = 1, (3) by weight-26-coefficients, (4) by companion-weight-82 and gross-companion-criterion.

items.name: Remark 2.5: a level-one representation of Sp_104
items.statement: Combining Theorem 2.4 (n = 105) with [CKPSS04, Thm. 7.2], there is a globally generic, non-endoscopic, cuspidal automorphic representation of Sp_104/Q of level one and weight zero.
items.note: The self-dual π of GL_105 has L(s, π, Sym^2) with a pole at s = 1 (∧^2 cannot have one as 105 is odd); [CKPSS04, Thm 7.2] then gives a globally generic cuspidal σ of Sp_104(A) lifting to π. Level one for σ needs a local argument the remark does not give (source issue E8).

items.name: Remark 2.5: cuspidal cohomology of 𝒜_52
items.statement: If 𝒜_g is the moduli space of principally polarized abelian varieties of dimension g, then H^*_cusp(𝒜_52, C) ≠ 0.
items.note: 𝒜_52(C) = Sp_104(Z)\ℍ_52; a globally generic σ of weight zero has σ_∞ a generic discrete series with nonzero relative Lie algebra cohomology. Siegel moduli: PELModuli M3 and ShimuraVarieties V5. The remark adds that endoscopic tempered classes exist for much smaller g ([CR15, §1.24]); no precise statement is given.

items.name: The image of generic functoriality for Sp_2n
items.statement: [CKPSS04, Thm. 7.2] (Ginzburg–Rallis–Soudry): for G_n = Sp_2n (or SO_2n, n ≥ 2), any functorial lift Π of a globally generic cuspidal π to GL_N(A) has trivial central character and is an isobaric sum Π_1 ⊞ ⋯ ⊞ Π_d of pairwise distinct unitary self-dual cuspidal Π_i with L^T(s, Π_i, Sym^2) having a pole at s = 1; conversely every such Π is the lift of some globally generic cuspidal π.
items.locator: Remark 2.5, p. 515; read at Numdam (Publ. IHÉS 99)
items.note: Global only: it says nothing about local components of π at places where Π is unramified. Routed to ModularityAndLanglandsExtensions ML.5 (known functorial transfers).

items.name: Theorem 3.1
items.statement: Let p > 5 be a prime, and let f be an eigenform of level SL_2(Z) and weight 2 ≤ k < p such that (1) (k − 1, p + 1) = 1 and (2) f is non-ordinary at p. Then there exists a self-dual cuspidal automorphic representation π of GL_p/Q of level one and weight zero whose mod p Galois representation ρ̄_π: G_Q → GL_p(F̄_p) is isomorphic to Sym^{p−1}ρ̄_f.

items.name: Local shape of ρ̄_f for non-ordinary f
items.statement: If f is non-ordinary at p and 2 ≤ k ≤ p, then ρ̄_f|G_{Q_p} is absolutely irreducible and ρ̄_f|I_p ≅ ω_2^{k−1} ⊕ ω_2^{p(k−1)} (Fontaine; [Edixhoven, Thm 2.6]).
items.note: R20.3 proves the Edixhoven/Serre weight theorem 'with its local finite-flat/extension calculations', including the irreducible local case; the decomposition of AlgebraicModularFormsAndSerreWeights R15.4 records Edixhoven's Thms 2.5–2.6 as its local inputs.

items.name: Large image in the non-ordinary case
items.statement: Under the hypotheses of Theorem 3.1, ρ̄_f(G_Q) ⊇ SL_2(F_p). The projective image of ρ̄_f(I_{Q_p}) contains a cyclic subgroup of order p + 1 > 5, which rules out projective image A_4, S_4 or A_5; ρ̄_f is absolutely irreducible because ρ̄_f|G_{Q_p} is; and dihedral image is impossible: being unramified outside p it would be induced from Q(√p*), p* = (−1)^{(p−1)/2}p, so ρ̄_f|G_{Q_p} would be induced from Q_p(√p*) and invariant under twisting by ε̄^{(p−1)/2} = ω_2^{(p^2−1)/2}, which forces k ≡ (p+3)/2 mod (p+1), contradicting (k−1, p+1) = 1.
items.note: Checked: twist invariance of ω_2^{k−1} ⊕ ω_2^{p(k−1)} by ω_2^{(p^2−1)/2} holds exactly when k ≡ (p+3)/2 mod (p+1) (for example p = 79: true at k = 41, false at k = 38). Routed to ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations R01.4.

items.name: The Lubin–Tate characters of Q_{p^2}
items.statement: ε_2, ε_2': G_{Q_{p^2}} → Z̄_p^× are the two Lubin–Tate characters trivial on Art_{Q_{p^2}}(p) (conjugate under Gal(Q_{p^2}/Q_p)), and ω_2 is the reduction of ε_2, a fundamental character of level 2.
items.note: ω_2 is planned in ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations R01.2 (fundamental characters of level two); the characteristic-zero characters come from local class field theory (Tau Ceti ClassFieldTheory Layer 8) and are crystalline (PadicHodgeTheory R06.2). Routed with the Part II's local layer.

items.name: The local representations ρ_{n,m}
items.statement: For n, m ≥ 1, ρ_{n,m} := Sym^{n−1} Ind_{G_{Q_{p^2}}}^{G_{Q_p}} ε_2^{−m}: G_{Q_p} → GL_n(Z̄_p), which is crystalline with Hodge–Tate weights 0, m, …, (n−1)m.

items.name: Reduction of ρ_{p,m}
items.note: On G_{Q_{p^2}} the constituents of Sym^{p−1}(ω_2^{−m} ⊕ ω_2^{−mp}) are ω_2^{−m(p−1)(1+j)}, j = 0, …, p−1; the pairs j, p−1−j give the inductions and j = (p−1)/2 the character ε̄^{m(p−1)/2}.

items.name: ρ̄_{p,m} does not depend on m
items.statement: If (m, p + 1) = 1 (so m is odd), then ω_2^{m(1−p)} has order exactly p + 1, the Gal(Q_{p^2}/Q_p)-conjugate of ω_2^{m(1−p)i} is ω_2^{−m(1−p)i}, and there is an isomorphism of orthogonal representations ρ̄_{p,m} ≅ ρ̄_{p,1}.
items.note: Checked: the multisets of exponents of ω_2 agree for all m < 3(p+1) prime to p+1, for p = 13 and p = 79.

items.name: ρ̄|G_{Q_p} in the non-ordinary case
items.statement: Under the hypotheses of Theorem 3.1 (f non-ordinary, k < p, (k−1, p+1) = 1), ρ̄|G_{Q_p} ≅ ρ̄_{p,1} for ρ̄ = Sym^{p−1}ρ̄_f, which admits the weight-zero crystalline lift ρ_{p,1}.
items.note: ρ̄_f|G_{Q_p} is induced from a level-2 character restricting to ω_2^{k−1} on inertia, up to an unramified quadratic twist, which Sym^{p−1} kills (p − 1 is even). So ρ̄|G_{Q_p} ≅ ρ̄_{p,m} with m ≡ ±(k−1) mod p^2 − 1, the sign depending on the normalisation of ω_2; either way (m, p+1) = (k−1, p+1) = 1, and rho-bar-p-m-independent gives ρ̄_{p,m} ≅ ρ̄_{p,1}.

items.name: The deformation ring R of Theorem 3.1
items.statement: R is the universal deformation ring for GO_p-valued deformations of ρ̄ = Sym^{p−1}ρ̄_f with multiplier ε^{1−p}, unramified outside p, whose restrictions to G_{Q_p} are crystalline of weight zero (Hodge–Tate weights 0, …, p−1) and lie on the same component of the local crystalline deformation ring as ρ_{p,1}. Every irreducible component of R has Krull dimension at least 1, by [BG19, Prop. 4.2.6].
items.note: H^0(Q, so_p^*(1)) = 0 as in Theorem 2.1; the oddness hypothesis is not discussed (source issue E5).

items.name: Auxiliary fields and the characters θ, θ′
items.statement: F^+/Q real quadratic with p inert; F/F^+ an imaginary CM quadratic extension in which the place above p splits, with F/Q disjoint from Q̄^{ker ρ̄}(ζ_p). As in the proof of [BLGGT14, Prop. 4.1.1], using [BLGGT14, Cor. A.2.3, Lem. A.2.5]: a cyclic CM extension M/F of degree k − 1 and characters θ, θ′: G_M → Q̄_p^× with θ̄ = θ̄′ such that s̄ := Ind_{G_M}^{G_F}(θ̄ ⊗ ρ̄|G_M) is absolutely irreducible; θθ^c = ε^{2−k}, θ′(θ′)^c = ε^{p(2−k)}; Ind θ and Ind θ′ crystalline with all sets of labelled Hodge–Tate weights {0, 1, …, k−2} and {0, p, …, p(k−2)} respectively; and, after replacing F^+ by a solvable extension, (Ind θ)|G_{F_v} ∼ ρ_{k−1,1}|G_{F_v} and (Ind θ′)|G_{F_v} ∼ ρ_{k−1,p}|G_{F_v} for every v | p.
items.locator: Proof of Theorem 3.1, p. 517 (the paper prints ρ̄|G_F inside the induction; see source issue E4)
items.note: Consistency checked: at a place w | v of M (M_w = F_v ⊇ Q_{p^2}) take θ_w with labelled weights (k−2−j, j) and θ′_w with (pj, p(k−2−j)); their reductions agree because ω_2^{p^2} = ω_2, and they match the constituents of ρ_{k−1,1} and ρ_{k−1,p}.

items.name: Auxiliary CM extensions and characters
items.statement: [BLGGT14, Cor. A.2.3]: for F imaginary CM, S a finite set of places, F^{(avoid)}/F finite Galois and N ≥ 1, there is a cyclic CM extension E/F of degree N in which every element of S splits completely, linearly disjoint from F^{(avoid)}. [BLGGT14, Lem. A.2.5]: for l prime, S ∋ all primes above l with S^c = S, a character χ of G_{F^+} and local characters ψ_v (v ∈ S, de Rham at v | l) with (ψ_vψ_{cv}^c)|I_{F_v} = χ|I_{F_v}: (1) if the places of S are unramified over F^+ and χ(c_v) is independent of v | ∞, there is θ with θθ^c = χ|G_F and θ|I_{F_v} = ψ_v|I_{F_v}; (2) for l > 2 and a residual θ̄ with θ̄θ̄^c = χ̄|G_F and θ̄|G_{F_v} = ψ̄_v, such a θ can be chosen lifting θ̄.
items.locator: Proof of Theorem 3.1, p. 517; read in [BLGGT14] arXiv v4, Appendix A.2

items.name: 'Connects' and its compatibilities
items.statement: [BLGGT14, §1.4]: continuous ρ_1, ρ_2: G_K → GL_n(O_{Q̄_l}) connect (ρ_1 ∼ ρ_2) if they have equivalent reductions, are potentially crystalline with the same labelled Hodge–Tate weights, and define points of the same irreducible component of Spec(R^□_{ρ̄,{HT_τ},K′−cris} ⊗ Q̄_l) for large K′. It is an equivalence relation compatible with restriction to finite extensions, direct sums, tensor products and duals, and with twisting by unramified characters with trivial reduction.
items.locator: Proof of Theorem 3.1, p. 517; read in [BLGGT14] arXiv v4, §1.4
items.note: Routed to LocalGaloisDeformationRings L7 (components of potentially semistable deformation rings). The compatibility with symmetric powers used implicitly in Theorem 3.1 follows because the components of these generic fibres are connected components and Sym^{p−1} induces a morphism of generic fibres.

items.name: The tensor identities on G_{F_v}
items.statement: For every place v | p of F (so F_v ⊇ Q_{p^2}): (ρ_{k−1,p} ⊗ ρ_{p,1})|G_{F_v} ≅ ρ_{(k−1)p,1}|G_{F_v} ≅ (ρ_{p,k−1} ⊗ ρ_{k−1,1})|G_{F_v}.
items.note: On G_{Q_{p^2}} each side is a sum of characters ε_2^{−a}(ε_2′)^{−b}; checked as multisets of (a, b) for (p, k) = (79, 38) and (13, 6). The second identity reindexes t = (k−1)j + l and the first t = j + pl.

items.name: The deformation ring R_F of Theorem 3.1
items.statement: R_F is the universal deformation ring for 𝒢_{(k−1)p}-valued deformations of the usual extension of s̄ with multiplier ε^{1−(k−1)p}δ_{F/F^+}, unramified outside p, whose restrictions to the places above p are crystalline with Hodge–Tate weights 0, 1, …, (k−1)p − 1 and lie on the same irreducible components of the local crystalline deformation rings as the representations of PAPER-BOXER-CALEGARI-GEE-25/tensor-identities.

items.name: The finite map R_F → R
items.statement: There is a finite map R_F → R taking a lifting ρ of ρ̄ to Ind_{G_M}^{G_F}(θ′ ⊗ ρ|G_M).
items.locator: Proof of Theorem 3.1, p. 517 (printed with θ and ρ|G_F; see source issue E4)
items.note: With θ′ the induced representation has multiplier ε^{p(2−k)}ε^{1−p} = ε^{1−(k−1)p} and regular Hodge–Tate weights {pa + b} = {0, …, (k−1)p − 1}; with θ, as printed, it has multiplier ε^{3−k−p} and repeated weights (checked for p = 79, k = 38).

items.name: Minimal finiteness with Thorne's 2017 adequacy
items.statement: [Tho12, Thm. 10.1] with [Tho17, Prop. 7.2]: F imaginary CM, l odd, S a finite set of places of F^+ containing those above l and split in F; (π, χ) RAECSDC of weight ι*λ unramified outside S, ρ a lattice in r_{l,ι}(π) with ρ̄ absolutely irreducible, extended to r̄: G_{F^+} → 𝒢_n(k) with ν∘r̄ = μ̄ε̄^{1−n}δ^κ; for v ∈ S choose irreducible components C_v of the local lifting rings (crystalline of weight λ at v | l) such that ρ|G_{F_ṽ} lies on no other. If ρ̄(G_{F(ζ_l)}) is adequate and ζ_l ∉ F, then κ = 0 and R_S^univ is a finite O-module; by [Tho17, Prop. 7.2] (which replaces [Tho12, Prop. 4.4] by [Tho17, Prop. 7.1] in the proofs of [Tho12, Thms 6.8, 8.6]) this holds with adequacy in the sense of [Tho17, Defn 2.20], including p | n.
items.locator: Proof of Theorem 3.1, p. 517; read in [Tho12] (author's copy; arXiv 1107.5989v1) and [Tho17] (author's copy dated 16 March 2016)

items.name: Automorphy lifting with Thorne's 2017 adequacy
items.statement: [Tho17, Thm. 5.1] (equivalently [Tho12, Thm. 7.1] in the form of [Tho17, Cor. 7.3]): let F be an imaginary CM field, ρ: G_F → GL_n(Q̄_p) with ρ^c ≅ ρ^∨ε^{1−n}, ρ̄(G_{F(ζ_p)}) adequate in the sense of [Tho17, Defn 2.20], ρ almost everywhere unramified, and a RACSDC π of GL_n(A_F) with r_ι(π)¯ ≅ ρ̄ and r_ι(π)|G_{F_v} ∼ ρ|G_{F_v} at every finite place v (plus a strong residual oddness condition when p = 2 and n is even). Then ρ is automorphic.
items.locator: Proof of Theorem 3.1, pp. 517–518 (cited as [Tho17, Thm. 7.1]; see source issue E3)
items.note: In Theorem 3.1 the seed π is the automorphic induction of the base change of Sym^{p−1}π_f twisted by θ, as in the proof of [BLGGT14, Prop. 4.1.1]; its local components connect to ρ_{p,k−1} ⊗ ρ_{k−1,1}.

items.name: Adequacy can be relaxed to H^1(H, ad) = 0
items.statement: In [Tho17, Defn. 2.20] the condition H^1(H, ad_0) = 0 can be replaced by the weaker H^1(H, ad) = 0: the proof of [Tho17, Prop. 2.21] only uses the weaker assumption. So the results of PAPER-BOXER-CALEGARI-GEE-25/thorne-minimal-finiteness and thorne-automorphy-lifting hold for this relaxed notion.
items.note: Checked in the author's copy of Tho17: the proofs of Prop. 2.21 and of Prop. 7.1 (the odd-l statement used through Prop. 7.2) use H^1(H, K) = 0 (no p-power quotient), H^1(H, ad) = 0 and the trace condition. Given H^1(H, K) = 0, H^1(H, ad_0) = 0 implies H^1(H, ad) = 0, so the new condition is weaker.

items.name: Adequacy of tensor products
items.statement: [BLGG13, Lem. A.3.1]: if r_1(Γ) is adequate, r_2|ker r_1 is irreducible and r_2(Γ) has order prime to l, then (r_1 ⊗ r_2)(Γ) is adequate. Its proof goes over for the relaxed notion, so since ρ̄(G_{Q(ζ_p)}) is adequate and p ∤ (k − 1), s̄(G_{F(ζ_p)}) is adequate.
items.locator: Proof of Theorem 3.1, p. 518; read in arXiv 1106.5586v1, Appendix A.3
items.note: The fourth-condition step of the proof yields exactly H^1(H, ad(r_1 ⊗ r_2)) = 0 from H^1(H_1, ad r_1) = 0, which is why the relaxed notion is the natural one here (dim s̄ = (k−1)p is divisible by p).

items.name: Automorphy under algebraic twists
items.statement: [BLGGT14, Lem. 2.2.1]: for F CM or totally real and ψ an algebraic character of G_F (φ its transfer to G_{F^+}, or ψ^2 if F is totally real), (r, μ) is automorphic if and only if (r ⊗ ψ, μφ) is.

items.name: Soluble descent of automorphy
items.statement: [BLGGT14, Lem. 2.2.2]: for M/F a soluble Galois extension with M CM or totally real and (r, μ) polarized with r|G_M irreducible, (r, μ) is automorphic if and only if (r|G_M, μ|G_{M^+}) is.

items.name: Automorphy of an induced representation descends
items.statement: [BLGGT14, Lem. 2.2.4]: for F CM or totally real, M/F soluble Galois CM or totally real of degree m, r: G_M → GL_n(Q̄_l) irreducible and μ a character of G_{F^+}: if (Ind_{G_M}^{G_F} r, μ) is an automorphic polarized representation, then (r, μ|G_{M^+}) is automorphic and polarized.

items.name: The lift ρ of Theorem 3.1 and its automorphy
items.statement: R_F is finite over O ([Tho12, Thm. 10.1] with [Tho17, Prop. 7.2] and the relaxed adequacy), hence R is; it has a Q̄_p-point giving ρ: G_Q → GO_p(Q̄_p) lifting ρ̄, unramified outside p, with multiplier ε^{1−p}, crystalline with Hodge–Tate weights 0, …, p−1. Ind_{G_M}^{G_F}(θ′ ⊗ ρ|G_M) is automorphic, so ρ is automorphic by [BLGGT14, Lem. 2.2.1, 2.2.2, 2.2.4]; the resulting π has level one and weight zero.
items.note: The level-one conclusion at p needs local–global compatibility at l = p for all π_p (PAPER-BOXER-CALEGARI-GEE-25/lgc-at-p-all-pi); the paper does not address it (source issue E6).

items.name: Corollary 3.2
items.statement: There exists a self-dual cuspidal automorphic representation π of GL_79/Q of level one and weight zero.
items.note: Theorem 3.1 with p = 79, k = 38.

items.name: A non-ordinary form of weight 38 at 79
items.statement: There is a level-one eigenform f of weight k = 38 that is non-ordinary at p = 79 ([Gou01, CG13]), and (37, 79 + 1) = 1.
items.note: Verified: det(T_79 | S_38) ≡ 0 (mod 79) (T_79 ≡ U_79 mod 79, computed in the Miller basis), so an eigenform has a_79 in a prime above 79; (37, 80) = 1. Agrees with [Gou01, Table 1] (79: weights 38, 44, …) and [CG13] (79: N[38]).

items.name: Remark 3.3: the smallest non-ordinary primes
items.statement: p = 79 is the second smallest prime for which there is a non-ordinary level-one eigenform of weight k < p; the smallest is p = 59, with a non-ordinary eigenform of weight 16, where (k − 1, p + 1) = (15, 60) ≠ 1.

items.name: Remark 3.3: primes where the theorems apply
items.statement: Level-one eigenforms satisfying the hypotheses of Theorem 3.1 exist for p = 79, 151, 173, 193, …, and eigenforms satisfying the hypotheses of Theorem 2.1 exist for p = 107, 139, 173, 179, … (the paper also lists 151; see source issue E7).
items.note: Theorem 3.1 list verified up to 193 from the non-ordinary pairs with (k−1, p+1) = 1. For Theorem 2.1, a search for companion pairs (k, p+1−k) matching T_2 and T_3 finds them for 101 ≤ p ≤ 193 only at p = 107 (26, 82), 139 (20, 120), 151 (52, 100), 173 (68, 106), 179 (30, 150), 191 (30, 162) and 193 (48, 146), agreeing with [CG13]; at 151, (150, 51) = (150, 99) = 3. Self-matches at k = (p+1)/2 (for instance (52, 52) at p = 103) are left aside: there (p−1, k−1) = (p−1)/2 ≠ 1 in any case.
